meanings.usage: 指研究恒星、星系等天体的科学
表示通过仪器或方法发现或感知某物的存在
指由众多恒星、气体和尘埃组成的巨大天体系统
指生物或事物经过漫长时间逐渐发展变化
常与of连用，表示有能力做某事
指天体运行的路径，或绕某天体运行的动作
指包围地球的气体层，或某地的一般氛围
指产生某种物质、能量或结果
指思想、活动或知识的领域或范围
blot out表示遮住、挡住光线
正式用语，指尝试做某事或努力做的事

examples.en: In relative terms, planets are very small and do not emit light.
examples.zh: 相对而言，行星非常小且不发光。

examples.en: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
examples.zh: 行星必须离它很远才能维持生命。

examples.en: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than 'little green men'.
examples.zh: 首先，我们会寻找植物生命，而不是小绿人。

examples.en: But this hope is always in the realms of science fiction.
examples.zh: 但这种希望总是在科幻小说的领域里。

examples.en: We would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star.
examples.zh: 我们必须找到一种方法遮住它恒星的光。

examples.en: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life.
examples.zh: 首先，我们会寻找植物生命。

examples.en: Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
examples.zh: 金星太热而火星太冷，都无法维持生命。

phrases.phrase: take + 时间 + for + 事物 + to do

examples.en: It has taken more than four billion years for plant and animal life to evolve.
examples.zh: 动植物生命进化花了四十多亿年。

examples.en: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
examples.zh: 用地面望远镜寻找另一颗行星上的生命是不可能的。

examples.en: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
examples.zh: 正是细菌产生了我们呼吸的氧气。

grammar.title: 虚拟语气 (Subjunctive Mood) - 与现在事实相反
grammar.structure: If + 主语 + were + 其他, 主语 + would/could/might + 动词原形
grammar.definition: 虚拟语气用于表达与事实相反的假设情况。使用were来表示与现在事实相反的假设 用于表达不太可能实现的假设或与事实相反的情况

examples.en: If we were able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
examples.zh: 如果我們能夠在另一颗行星上发现像细菌这样的低等生命，那将完全改变我们对自己的看法。

grammar.title: 定语从句 (Relative Clause) - 关系副词where引导
grammar.structure: 名词 + where + 完整句子
grammar.definition: 用where引导的定语从句修饰表示地点的名词，说明事件发生的场所 where在从句中作地点状语，修饰其前的名词

examples.en: A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter to look for life in outer space, where the dust becomes thinner.
examples.zh: 望远镜必须远到像木星那样的距离才能在外太空寻找生命，那里的尘埃更稀薄。

grammar.title: 强调句型 (Emphatic Structure) - It is/was + 被强调部分 + that/who + 其他
grammar.structure: It is/was + 强调部分 + that/who + 句子其他部分
grammar.definition: 使用It is/was...that/who...结构强调句子的某个成分 可用于强调主语、宾语或状语，增强表达效果

examples.en: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
examples.zh: 正是细菌产生了我们呼吸的氧气。

original.en: Whether a planet can support life depends on the size and brightness of its star.
original.zh: 行星是否能维持生命取决于其恒星的大小和亮度。

imitations.en: Whether we can find water on Mars depends on its geological conditions.
imitations.zh: 我们能否在火星上找到水取决于它的地质条件。

imitations.en: Whether the plan will succeed depends on everyone's cooperation.
imitations.zh: 这个计划是否成功取决于每个人的配合。

patterns.pattern: The first question to answer is whether...

original.en: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.
original.zh: 首先要回答的问题是行星是否真的能维持生命。

imitations.en: The first problem to solve is whether we have enough funding.
imitations.zh: 首先要解决的问题是我们是否有足够的资金。

imitations.en: The first step to take is whether we should accept their offer.
imitations.zh: 首先要采取的步骤是我们是否应该接受他们的提议。

patterns.pattern: It is + adj + to do something

original.en: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
original.zh: 用地面望远镜寻找另一颗行星上的生命是不可能的。

imitations.en: It is difficult to detect planets in distant galaxies.
imitations.zh: 探测遥远星系中的行星是困难的。

imitations.en: It is necessary to understand the basic principles of astronomy.
imitations.zh: 理解天文学的基本原理是必要的。

patterns.pattern: A planet would have to be...to be capable of...

original.en: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
original.zh: 行星必须离它很远才能维持生命。

imitations.en: An organism would have to adapt to extreme conditions to be capable of surviving.
imitations.zh: 有机体必须适应极端条件才能存活。

imitations.en: A telescope would have to be placed in space to be capable of detecting small objects.
imitations.zh: 望远镜必须放置在太空中才能探测到小物体。

lines.en: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our won Milky Way and in other galaxies .
lines.zh: 天文学方面最新发展使得我们能够在银河系和其他星系发现行星。

lines.en: This is a major achievement because, in relative terms, planets are very small and old not emit light.
lines.zh: 这是一个重要的成就，因为相对来说，行星很小，而且也不发光。

lines.en: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.
lines.zh: 寻找行星证明相当困难，但是要在行星上发现生命会变得无比艰难。

lines.en: The first question to answer is whether a planet can actually support life.
lines.zh: 第一个需要解答的问题是一颗行星是否有能够维持生命的条件。

lines.en: In our won solar system, for example, Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
lines.zh: 举例来说，在我们的太阳系里，对于生命来说，金星的温度太高，而火星的温度则太低。

lines.en: Only the Earth provides ideal conditions, and even here it has taken more than four billion years for plant and animal life to evolve.
lines.zh: 只有地球提供理想的条件，而即使在这里，植物和动物的进化也用了40亿年的时间。

lines.en: Whether a planet can support life depends on the size and brightness of its star, that is its 'sun'.
lines.zh: 一颗行星是否能够维持生命取决于它的恒星——即它的“太阳”——的大小和亮度。

lines.en: Imagine a star up t twenty times larger, brighter, brighter and hotter than our own sun.
lines.zh: 设想一下，一颗恒星比我们的太阳还要大，还要亮，还要热20倍，那么一颗行星为了维持生命就要离开的它的恒星非常远。

lines.en: A planet would have to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
lines.zh: 反之，如果恒星很小，维持生命的行星就要在离恒星很近的轨道上运行，而且要有极好的条件才能使生命得以发展，但是，我们如何才能找到这样一颗行星呢？

lines.en: Alternatively, if the star were small, the life-supporting planet would have to have a close orbit round it and also provide the perfect conditions for life forms to develop.
lines.zh: 现在，没有一台现存的望远镜可以发现生命的存在。

lines.en: But how would we find such a planet?
lines.zh: 而开发这样一台望远镜将会是21世纪天文学的一个重要的研究课题。

lines.en: At present, there is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.
lines.zh: 使用放置在地球上的望远镜是无法观察到其他行星的生命的。

lines.en: The development of such a telescope will be one of the great astronomical projects of the twenty-first century.
lines.zh: 地球周围温暖的大气层和望远镜散出的热量使得我们根本不可能找到比行星更小的物体。

lines.en: It is impossible to look for life on another planet using earth-based telescopes.
lines.zh: 即使是一台放置在围绕地球的轨道上的望远镜——如非常成功的哈勃望远镜——也因为太阳系中的尘埃微粒而无法胜任。

lines.en: Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
lines.zh: 望远镜要放置在木星那样遥远的行星上才有可能在外层空间搜寻生命。

lines.en: Even a telescope in orbit round the earth, like the very successful Hubble telescope, would not be suitable because of the dust particles iron solar system.
lines.zh: 因为我们越是接近太阳系的边缘，尘埃就越稀薄。

lines.en: A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter to look for life in outer space, because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our own solar system.
lines.zh: 一旦我们找到这样一颗行星，我们就要想办法将它的恒星射过来的光线遮暗，这样我们就能彻底“看见”这颗行星，并分析它的大气层。

lines.en: Once we detected a planet, we would have to find a way of blotting out the light from its star, so that we would be able to 'see' the planet properly and analyze its atmosphere.
lines.zh: 首先我们要寻找植物，而不是那种“小绿人”。

lines.en: In the first instance, we would be looking for plant life, rather than 'little green men'.
lines.zh: 行星上最容易生存下来的是细菌。

lines.en: The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.
lines.zh: 正是细菌生产出我们在地球上呼吸的氧气。

lines.en: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
lines.zh: 在地球上发展的大部分进程中，细菌是地球上唯一的生命形式。

lines.en: For most of the earth's history they have been the only form of life on our planet.
lines.zh: 作为地球上的居民，我们总存有这样的希望：小绿人来拜访我们，而我们可以和他们交流。

lines.en: As Earth-dwellers, we always cherish the hope that we will be visited by little green men and that we will be able to communicate with them.
lines.zh: 但是，这种希望总是只在科幻小说中存在。

lines.en: But this hope is always in the realms of science fiction.
lines.zh: 如果我们能够在另一颗行星上找到诸如细菌的那种低等生命，那么这个发现将彻底改变我们对我们自己的看法。

lines.en: If we were able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
lines.zh: 正如美国国家航空和宇宙航空局的丹尼尔。

lines.en: As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, 'Finding life elsewhere would change everything.
lines.zh: 戈尔丁指出的“在其他地方发现生命会改变一切。

lines.en: No human endeavor or thought would be unchanged by it."
lines.zh: 任何人类的努力和想法都会发生变化。”

questions.q: Which life forms are most likely to develop on a distant planet?
questions.zh: 在遥远的行星上，最有可能发展出哪种生命形式？
questions.hint: 见课文倒数第五、六句：The life forms most likely to develop on a planet would be bacteria.

questions.q: Why can't Venus or Mars support life?
questions.zh: 为什么金星或火星都不能维持生命？
questions.a: Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
questions.aZh: 金星实在太热，而火星又实在太冷，都无法维持生命。
questions.hint: 见课文第五句：Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.

questions.q: Why are earth-based telescopes unable to detect life on other planets?
questions.zh: 为什么设在地球上的望远镜无法探测其他行星上的生命？
questions.a: Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope would make it impossible to detect objects as small as planets.
questions.aZh: 我们周围温暖的大气层以及望远镜产生的热量，使我们无法探测像行星那样小的物体。
questions.hint: 见课文第十三句：Our own warm atmosphere and the heat generated by the telescope…

questions.q: How far away would a telescope have to be to look for life in outer space?
questions.zh: 要在外层空间寻找生命，望远镜得放到多远的地方？
questions.a: It would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter, because the dust becomes thinner the further we travel towards the outer edges of our solar system.
questions.aZh: 它得放到木星那样远，因为我们越接近太阳系的边缘，尘埃就越稀薄。
questions.hint: 见课文第十五句：A telescope would have to be as far away as the planet Jupiter…

questions.q: What would it mean if we discovered lowly life like bacteria on another planet?
questions.zh: 如果在另一颗行星上发现像细菌这样的低等生命，那意味着什么？
questions.a: It would completely change our view of ourselves. As Daniel Goldin of NASA observed, 'Finding life elsewhere would change everything.'
questions.aZh: 它会彻底改变我们对自己的看法。正如美国国家航空航天局的戈尔丁所说：'在其他地方发现生命会改变一切。'
questions.hint: 见课文最后两句，作者用 Danie Goldin 的话作总结。

translation:
天文学方面最新发展使得我们能够在银河系和其他星系发现行星。
这是一个重要的成就，因为相对来说，行星很小，而且也不发光。
寻找行星证明相当困难，但是要在行星上发现生命会变得无比艰难。
第一个需要解答的问题是一颗行星是否有能够维持生命的条件。
举例来说，在我们的太阳系里，对于生命来说，金星的温度太高，而火星的温度则太低。
只有地球提供理想的条件，而即使在这里，植物和动物的进化也用了40亿年的时间。
一颗行星是否能够维持生命取决于它的恒星——即它的“太阳”——的大小和亮度。
设想一下，一颗恒星比我们的太阳还要大，还要亮，还要热20倍，那么一颗行星为了维持生命就要离开的它的恒星非常远。
反之，如果恒星很小，维持生命的行星就要在离恒星很近的轨道上运行，而且要有极好的条件才能使生命得以发展，但是，我们如何才能找到这样一颗行星呢？
现在，没有一台现存的望远镜可以发现生命的存在。
而开发这样一台望远镜将会是21世纪天文学的一个重要的研究课题。
使用放置在地球上的望远镜是无法观察到其他行星的生命的。
地球周围温暖的大气层和望远镜散出的热量使得我们根本不可能找到比行星更小的物体。
即使是一台放置在围绕地球的轨道上的望远镜——如非常成功的哈勃望远镜——也因为太阳系中的尘埃微粒而无法胜任。
望远镜要放置在木星那样遥远的行星上才有可能在外层空间搜寻生命。
因为我们越是接近太阳系的边缘，尘埃就越稀薄。
一旦我们找到这样一颗行星，我们就要想办法将它的恒星射过来的光线遮暗，这样我们就能彻底“看见”这颗行星，并分析它的大气层。
首先我们要寻找植物，而不是那种“小绿人”。
行星上最容易生存下来的是细菌。
正是细菌生产出我们在地球上呼吸的氧气。
在地球上发展的大部分进程中，细菌是地球上唯一的生命形式。
作为地球上的居民，我们总存有这样的希望：小绿人来拜访我们，而我们可以和他们交流。
但是，这种希望总是只在科幻小说中存在。
如果我们能够在另一颗行星上找到诸如细菌的那种低等生命，那么这个发现将彻底改变我们对我们自己的看法。
正如美国国家航空和宇宙航空局的丹尼尔。
戈尔丁指出的“在其他地方发现生命会改变一切。
任何人类的努力和想法都会发生变化。”
title: From the Earth: Greetings
subtitle: 来自地球的问候

lead.question: 在遥远行星上，最有可能发展出哪一种生命形式？
lead.warmup: 天文学家近来已能在银河系乃至其他星系里发现行星，这是了不起的成就，因为行星既小又不发光。可要在行星上找到生命，就更加困难。本课先谈'什么样的行星能维持生命'，再谈寻找生命所需的望远镜，最后落到最可能出现的生命形式——细菌。
goals: 掌握 astronomy、planet、galaxy、telescope 等天文词汇
理解 be capable of doing 与 make it possible to do 的用法
体会虚拟语气 would have to / if...were 在假设句中的表达
学会用强调句 It is...that... 和定语从句突出信息
lead.summary: 课文从天文学的进展说起：行星渺小又不发光，探测本已不易，寻找其上的生命更是难上加难。行星能否维持生命，取决于它那颗恒星的大小与亮度，离恒星太近或太远都不行。地球上的望远镜难以胜任，因为大气和镜身发热，还有尘埃干扰。科学家设想先去找植物，而最可能发展出来的其实是细菌——正是细菌造出了我们呼吸的氧气。
lead.tips: 易错提醒：make it possible to do 中的 it 是形式宾语，真正宾语是后面的不定式，切勿漏掉 it。

exercises.q: 汉译英：找到行星已经够难了，但要在它们上面找到生命会难得多。
exercises.a: Finding planets is proving hard enough, but finding life on them will prove infinitely more difficult.
exercises.note: 动名词作主语，infinitely 修饰比较级。

exercises.q: 句型转换：改为强调句，强调 bacteria。Bacteria have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.
exercises.a: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe on earth.

exercises.q: 填空：A planet ___ (have) to be a very long way from it to be capable of supporting life.
改错：In our own solar system, Venus is very too hot to support life.
exercises.a: In our own solar system, Venus is far too hot to support life.
exercises.note: 用 far too，不用 very too。

exercises.q: 汉译英：天文学方面最新发展使得我们能够在银河系和其他星系发现行星。
exercises.a: Recent developments in astronomy have made it possible to detect planets in our own Milky Way and in other galaxies.
exercises.note: make it possible to do 形式宾语。

exercises.q: 句型转换：合并为含定语从句的一句。There is no telescope in existence. It is capable of detecting the presence of life.
exercises.a: There is no telescope in existence that is capable of detecting the presence of life.
exercises.note: that 引导定语从句，capable of doing。

exercises.q: 填空：If we ___ (be) able to discover lowly forms of life like bacteria on another planet, it would completely change our view of ourselves.
exercises.note: 与现在事实相反的虚拟语气。

quiz.q: 课文提到，除地球之外，太阳系中的行星为何不适合生命？
options: Venus is far too hot and Mars is far too cold to support life.
Venus is far too cold and Mars is far too hot to support life.
Both are far too far away from the sun.
Neither of them has enough water on it.

quiz.q: 一颗行星能否维持生命取决于什么？
options: The size and brightness of its star.
The number of moons going round it.
How close it is to the Earth.
The colour of its sun in the sky.
quiz.note: 取决于恒星大小与亮度。

quiz.q: 为什么设在地球上的望远镜无法探测像行星这样小的天体？
options: Our atmosphere and the telescope's own heat make it impossible.
Planets never emit any light at all in space.
Telescopes are simply too small to be of use.
Dust in space blocks all light for ever.

quiz.q: 要在外层空间寻找生命，望远镜至少要放到多远？
options: As far away as the planet Jupiter.
Only just beyond the moon.
As far as the nearest galaxy.
A few hundred kilometres above the earth.

quiz.q: 课文中，最可能在行星上发展出来的生命形式是什么？
options: Bacteria.
Little green men.
Large mammals.
Flowering plants.

quiz.q: 关于地球上我们呼吸的氧气，课文怎么说？
options: It is bacteria that have generated the oxygen we breathe.
Oxygen was brought here by passing comets.
Plants produced oxygen long before bacteria did.
There was no oxygen until humans appeared.
